# gba-emu: rules for every agent

Read PLAN.md before starting. It defines the phases, the shared contracts and who owns which file.
The benchmark lives at `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-eval`, referred to below as `$GBA_EVAL`.
Use that absolute path; relative paths break inside worktrees.

## Originality (hard rule)
- Write all code yourself. Do not read, copy, or paraphrase any existing emulator:
  `$GBA_EVAL/candidates/` (gba-core), `$GBA_EVAL/third_party/` (Mesen2),
  `$GBA_EVAL/reference/mesen_step.cpp`, or mGBA/NanoBoyAdvance/VBA/etc. from memory or the web.
- Allowed sources: `$GBA_EVAL/spec/gbatek.htm` (GBA, ARM and THUMB chapters only), `$GBA_EVAL/spec/ABI.md`,
  `$GBA_EVAL/spec/gba_bios_stub.h`, the grader's outputs (scores, `.ref.png` vs `.cand.png`),
  and running ROMs from `$GBA_EVAL/corpus/roms/`.
- No per-ROM hacks: never branch on a ROM's hash, title, or game code. Fix the hardware behavior.

## Code readability
- Use clear, descriptive names for functions, variables and types: `destination_register`, `shift_amount`,
  `fn execute_data_processing`. Never cryptic ones like `x`, `t`, `rd2` or `tmp`. Loop indices
  (`i`, `line`) are fine when the meaning is obvious.
- Official gbatek register and field names are allowed (`DISPCNT`, `BG0CNT`, `IE`, `IF`, `CPSR`, `Rd`, `Rn`),
  each with a short plain-English comment where it is defined, e.g. `const DISPCNT: u32 = 0x000; // display control`.
- Every non-obvious function gets a one-line doc comment naming the gbatek section it implements, e.g.
  `/// Barrel shifter for data-processing operand 2 (gbatek: ARM Opcodes: Data Processing (ALU)).`
- Prefer small readable functions over clever one-liners. Split a long `match` arm or a dense bit-twiddling
  expression into a named helper.

## Ownership
- Only edit the files your task owns (see the ownership tables in PLAN.md).
- Shared files (`src/lib.rs`, `src/gba.rs`, `src/bus.rs`, `src/io.rs`, `src/irq.rs`, `src/scheduler.rs`,
  `Cargo.toml`) are changed only by the integrator (the executor session). If you need a contract
  change, say so in your report instead of making it.

## Git
- Remote: https://github.com/Rohan-Jalil/gba-eval-trial-rohan. Never push; the human pushes.
- Author and committer: Rohan Jalil <[REDACTED:email]>. This is set in this repo's git config;
  do not override it.
- Use Conventional Commits: `type(scope): summary`, for example `feat(cpu): add ARM data-processing ops`,
  `fix(ppu): wrap affine BG coordinates`, `test(timer): cascade overflow`, `docs(notes): phase 1 decisions`,
  `chore(results): phase 1 milestone`. Scopes: cpu, arm, thumb, bus, io, irq, ppu, apu, dma, timer,
  keypad, cart, abi, scripts, plan, notes, results.
- Commit after every meaningful step (a working instruction group, a passing test, a merged branch),
  not one large commit per phase.
- Worker agents commit on their own branch. Only the integrator merges into `main` (`git merge --no-ff`).

## Logging
- `NOTES.md`: add an entry for every decision or change of approach (date, what, why), and for every
  phase record which agents ran and on which model. The integrator writes the agent/model rows.
- `TIMELOG.md` belongs to the human. Agents never edit it.
- Milestones: `scripts/grade-full.sh <phase> "<note>"` saves `results/milestones/<phase>/`. Commit that
  folder and `scores.tsv`. All other `results/` output stays ignored.

## Before you report done
1. `cargo test` passes.
2. `cargo build --release --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` succeeds.
3. `scripts/grade-subset.sh target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/gba_emu.wasm <name> <your tests> <smoke set>`.
   Report the per-test scores, and never lower a smoke-set score without saying so.
4. Your work is committed on your branch, and your report lists the commits.

content.text:
The branch is ready to merge. I found no blocker or major problems; the findings are below, most severe first.

**Scope and ownership.** The branch adds two commits, `fe3a38f` (affine backgrounds) and `c5362b8` (bitmap modes through the BG2 transform). They touch only `src/ppu/bg_affine.rs` and `src/ppu/bitmap.rs`, which the "Affine + bitmap" row of PLAN.md assigns to this worker.

**Checked against gbatek and found correct:**
- **BGxCNT fields:** priority (bits 0-1), character base in 16 KiB units (bits 2-3), screen base in 2 KiB units (bits 8-12), wraparound bit 13, and size bits 14-15 giving 128/256/512/1024 pixels.
- **Tiles and map:** affine backgrounds are always 256-colour, with one-byte map entries and 64 bytes per tile.
- **Area overflow:** with bit 13 clear, pixels outside the map are transparent. With it set, the map wraps; the code masks the coordinates, which also handles negative ones because the sizes are powers of two.
- **Bitmap modes:** the overflow bit is ignored and everything outside the bitmap is transparent ("This works only in BG modes 1 and 2... outside of the Bitmaps is always transparent").
- **Mode-specific rules:** mode 3 ignores the frame-select bit, modes 3 and 5 are never transparent, mode 4 index 0 is transparent, and mode 5 is 160x128.
- **Transform stepping:** each pixel steps by PA and PC from the internal reference point, which `mod.rs` advances by PB and PD per line and reloads at VBlank. The sign handling (20.8 fixed point, arithmetic `>> 8`) is right.

**Checks run** on main with this branch merged, in a scratch worktree that I removed afterwards:
- `cargo test`: 103 passed, 0 failed, and no compiler warnings.
- `cargo build --release --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`: succeeds.
- `run_rom` for 120 frames on the five ROMs the plan names for this role: `tonc/sbb-aff`, `tonc/m7-demo`, `tonc/bm-modes`, `tonc/pageflip` and `nba-hw/ppu-bgx`. All exit cleanly. Looking at the frames, `sbb-aff` and `m7-demo` render plausibly (the mode 7 floor tiles shrink toward the horizon as expected) and `ppu-bgx` is a solid green screen. I did not compare them against the reference images, and I did not run the grader, as instructed.

**Findings:**
- `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/src/ppu/bg_affine.rs:48` and `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/src/ppu/bitmap.rs:17`: [minor] Background mosaic (BGxCNT bit 6) is not applied in either renderer. It is flagged with a `ponytail:` comment that waits on the effects worker. Either the integrator tracks it as a follow-up, or it gets wired in when a mosaic helper exists.
- `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/src/ppu/bg_affine.rs:65-71`: [minor] The map-entry and pixel address calculations are dense one-line expressions. Splitting them into small named helpers, such as `affine_map_offset` and `tile_dot_offset`, would match the CLAUDE.md rule on dense expressions.
- `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/src/ppu/bg_affine.rs:14-15`: [minor] `AffineWalk.texture_x` and `texture_y` are `pub`, but every caller goes through `pixel()`. They should be private.
- `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/src/ppu/bitmap.rs:62-65`: [minor] The test renders the same line three times, and two of its asserts check the same thing (`color == 0` and `color != RED`). Render once and drop the duplicate assert.
- `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/src/ppu/bitmap.rs` and `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/src/ppu/bg_affine.rs` (tests): [minor] Some paths have no unit test: mode 4 palette lookup and frame select, BG3 (the second set of affine registers), and a pixel inside a tile other than (0,0). The named ROMs cover them partly; one small test each would be cheap.
- `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/src/ppu/mod.rs:283`: [minor, integrator-owned, not part of this diff] The `#[allow(dead_code)]` on `affine_reference_point` is stale now that this branch uses it. Remove it at merge time.

**Per-ROM hacks:** none. Nothing branches on a ROM hash, title, game code or a specific address.

**Originality:** the structure is simple and follows gbatek's terms directly (dx/dmx stepping, the overflow bit, the BGxCNT layout). There are no magic tables, no names that suggest another emulator, and the style matches the rest of the codebase.
